analysis.title: US Credit Strategy: A roadmap for AI CDS
key_insights: All ten members of Barclays' AI CDS cohort (six hyperscalers, four semiconductors) have widened over six months and trade near the wide end of their six-month ranges. The gap between the cohort average and CDX.IG rose from about 10bp six months ago to 76bp now, with 31bp of that since the September 21 CDS roll.
The ten AI issuers are 8% of CDX.IG constituents but 16% (about 10bp) of the index's intrinsic spread.

AI cohort CDS has underperformed maturity-matched cash bonds. The average CDS-cash basis for the AI cohort rose about 50bp over the year and is now positive, while the non-AI basis is little changed and remains negative.

Four-week average weekly CDS volume reached about $6bn for hyperscalers and $3bn for semiconductors as of October 23, up roughly 740% and 1,900% y/y, partly from low starting volumes. AI names were under 5% of Americas corporate single-name CDS volume a year ago, as much as 36% in August, and about 20% now.

Net notional open interest rose from about $5bn to $20bn for hyperscalers and from about $1.9bn to $8.6bn for semiconductors. The cohort is now nearly 14% of Americas corporate single-name CDS open interest, up from 4% a year ago.

The chip-financing names AVGO, AMD and NVDA traded in the low 40bp area six months ago and are now among the widest. AVGO widened most in percent terms (+258%). ORCL and SPCX are the widest names, while MSFT, the lone AAA credit, widened least (+9bp, +20%).

AMZN and GOOGL both trade at 80-81bp in 5y CDS, but AMZN's 3s5s curve has steepened only 2bp over six months and looks flat versus GOOGL's. Barclays links this to a June delayed-draw term loan (3-year maturity from draw date) that may have created technical buying at the 2.5-3.0y CDS points.

ORCL's 3s5s curve has flattened considerably over the past month and looks especially flat versus comps. AVGO's 3s5s is flat relative to its 5y spread versus AMD and NVDA. INTC's 3s5s looks steep, almost as steep in percentage terms as MSFT's.

The INTC CDS-cash basis is the only negative one in the cohort (-14bp). AMD (+29bp), AVGO (+28bp), ORCL (+24bp) and NVDA (+15bp) have the most positive bases. ORCL's basis is at the 80th percentile of its one-year range after retracing from the cohort's most positive level.
ORCL CDS lagged the cash rally on October 28 after the company announced more limited funding needs than expected.

DTCC data: ORCL ranks first among Americas corporate single-name CDS in both volume ($2.3bn 4-week average weekly) and open interest ($6.9bn). Six cohort names are in the top ten by volume and three in the top ten by net notional outstanding.

ICE cleared open interest is concentrated in the 4-5y area (85-90%) for MSFT, GOOGL, META, NVDA and SPCX. AMZN's largest share is in the June 2029 contract and INTC's in December 2029, so both carry more cleared risk in shorter maturities.

CoreWeave (CRWV), the only directly AI-related name in the on-the-run CDX.HY, has 5y CDS at 15.5 points upfront versus a six-month range of -2.3 to 20. 4-week average weekly volume rose to $302mn from $32mn, net notional to $850mn from $65mn, and 67% of cleared risk sits at 4-5y.
Trade recommendations: buy AVGO 5y CDS protection as a hedge for the broader AI funding overhang. Buy AMZN 5y CDS protection outright or put on a DV01-neutral 3s5s steepener. Sell the ORCL 5y basis.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays recommends buying AVGO 5y CDS protection to hedge the broader AI funding overhang. AVGO widened 258% in six months to 168bp, with a +28bp CDS-cash basis.

sector_views.rationale: Spreads have widened across the cohort and trade near the wide end of six-month ranges, with CDS underperforming cash. The trade recommendations are mostly protection buying, with relative value in ORCL basis.

trade_ideas.rationale: Hedge the broader AI funding overhang. AVGO is among the widest names after widening from the low 40bp area to 168bp.

trade_ideas.description: Buy AMZN 5y CDS protection outright, or put on a 3s5s steepener (sell 3y protection, buy 5y protection, DV01-neutral)
trade_ideas.rationale: AMZN's 3s5s curve looks flat versus GOOGL's, possibly from technical buying tied to a June delayed-draw term loan. The trade positions for curve normalization.

trade_ideas.description: Sell ORCL 5y basis: sell the 5.25s of 2032 versus selling 5y or 5.5y CDS protection
trade_ideas.rationale: ORCL's basis is still among the most positive in the cohort, and CDS lagged the cash rally on October 28 after Oracle announced more limited funding needs than expected. The trade positions for compression.

risk_factors: AI funding overhang is the stated reason to hold protection in AVGO.
Percentage volume increases partly reflect low starting volumes and newly developed CDS markets for several issuers.
ICE data capture only cleared positions and give a less complete view of risk outstanding than DTCC.
Matched bonds are not necessarily the most recent or most liquid bonds near five years, which affects basis comparisons.
charts_described: Figure 3 plots the spread differential between the AI cohort average and CDX.IG, widening from 10bp six months ago to 74-76bp, with the CDS-cash basis on the right axis.
Figure 14 shows the maturity-matched CDS-cash basis by issuer: INTC -14bp, SPCX +1, GOOGL +2, AMZN +3, MSFT +6, META +13, NVDA +15, ORCL +24, AVGO +28, AMD +29.
vol_and_positioning: AI cohort share of Americas corporate single-name CDS open interest is nearly 14%, up from 4% a year ago, and net notional exceeds $28bn.
Four-week average weekly CDS volume is $6bn for hyperscalers and $3bn for semiconductors.
Cleared risk at ICE is concentrated in 4-5y maturities for MSFT, GOOGL, META, NVDA and SPCX (85-90%), and more dispersed for AMZN, INTC, AMD, ORCL and AVGO.
